standard_prerequisites: Locally quasi-coherent sheaves with the flat base change property on an algebraic stack (Sheaves on Stacks / Cohomology of Stacks definitions)

Same-chapter lemma-is-limit (source 4990-5007): an object K of D(O_X) whose cohomology sheaves are locally quasi-coherent with flat base change is the derived limit of its canonical truncations tau_{>= -n} K
Direct sums vs products in derived categories; truncation of a direct sum of sheaves shifted in distinct degrees
core_obligations: Each F_n[n] has locally quasi-coherent cohomology sheaves (only one nonzero, in degree -n) satisfying the flat base change property, so lemma-is-limit applies to K = \oplus_n F_n[n]

The canonical truncations of K are the finite partial sums; the derived-limit triangle identifies K with the product of its truncations, and the resulting map is exactly \oplus_n F_n[n] -> \prod_n F_n[n]
Hence \oplus_n F_n[n] -> \prod_n F_n[n] is an isomorphism in D(O_X)
proof_roadmap: Check the hypotheses of lemma-is-limit for K = \oplus F_n[n]
Compute the canonical truncations as finite partial sums
Read the derived-limit isomorphism as the sum-to-product map
